intro: A fair balance between government, its workforce and the people it serves.
position: Yankee Institute advocates rebalancing Connecticut’s relationship with government unions, with public services and taxpayer accountability at the center.
context: Labor policy reaches beyond the negotiating table. It shapes the cost of public services, retirement obligations and the choices available to Connecticut communities.

questions.title: How should government serve residents?
questions.text: Yankee Institute argues that state and local government should be organized around services for residents, rather than treated as a jobs program.

questions.title: What do employment numbers tell us?
questions.text: Connecticut’s payroll job count and estimates of employed residents are moving in different directions. Portfolio explains the surveys’ differences and the warning signs obscured by the record payroll figure.

questions.title: Who pays for pension promises?
questions.text: The State Police overtime study examines how overtime practices affect pension obligations, and calls for extending reforms to employees covered by older rules.
